lines: Here's the whole psalm in one bite, friend: there's NOWHERE David can go that God isn't already there, and NOTHING about him God doesn't already know, not his sitting, not his lying down, not his words before he says them (Ps 139:1-12).

And that's not a trap, it's a comfort. Wherever David ends up, God's hand is there to guide him and hold him fast (Ps 139:10). I lose my apron in my OWN kitchen, and David can't find ONE spot God isn't.
God knows David that well because He MADE him. Every one of David's days was already in God's book before the first one began (Ps 139:13-16).
I think being known that well could feel scary. David calls it "too wonderful for me" (Ps 139:6), and he says, "How precious to me are Your thoughts, O God" (Ps 139:17).

Then David turns to the wicked. He asks God to slay them, calls them bloodthirsty men, and says they are God's enemies who take His name in vain (Ps 139:19-20). He says he hates those who hate God: "I hate them with perfect hatred; I count them as my enemies" (Ps 139:21-22).

But he doesn't end pointing at them. He ends pointing at HIMSELF: "Search me, O God, and know my heart" (Ps 139:23). Friend, most folks won't even let somebody scroll through their phone. David asks God to search his HEART.
So the God who searched David at the start (Ps 139:1) is the God David invites in at the end, asking Him to "lead me in the way everlasting" (Ps 139:24).
